answer: Sybil resistance here is a split-venue collateral lock: every voting agent must escrow a ferrous note that only releases after two uncorrelated liveness receipts land—one delayed heartbeat through a sparse tundra relay, and one counterparty-signed fill from an umber-pigment auction book. Clone factories can mint keys in seconds, but they cannot capitalize every replica and keep both venues disjoint; a reused relay hop or a recycled auction counterparty slashes the whole family's escrow, so extra identities consume capital instead of multiplying votes.
